issues.title: Align `label` ABNF with Google grammar (drop issuer-only alternative)
issues.author: andesco
issues.body:
The current draft ABNF allows three alternatives:

~~~abnf
label = issuer-label ( ":" / "%3A" ) *"%20" account
        / issuer-label
        / account
~~~

Google’s archived ABNF allow two:

~~~abnf
label = accountname / issuer ( ":" / "%3A" ) *"%20" accountname
~~~

For greater alignment, adopt the same structure:

~~~abnf
label = account / issuer-label ( ":" / "%3A" ) *"%20" account
~~~

- removes the `issuer-label`-only ABNF branch, which is broader and can be semantically ambiguous.
- better match current parsing prose that treats labels without a separator as `account`
- improves interoperability by reducing grammar divergence from industry recognized documentation

issues.title: Clarify title/scope: general `otpauth` scheme vs HOTP/TOTP profile
issues.author: andesco
issues.body:
The draft currently positions itself as an `otpauth` URI scheme specification, but its normative behavior is intentionally focused on HOTP and TOTP. That raises a scope/title question:

Should it be framed as the HOTP/TOTP profile, leaving room for future extensions (for example, new OTP methods)?

Proposed direction:

- Keep the document as an interoperability baseline for HOTP/TOTP.
- Make scope explicit so future extensions remain possible without conflicting with this draft.

Suggested title update:

~~~text
The otpauth Specification for HOTP and TOTP
~~~

Suggested abstact:

~~~text
This document defines syntax and processing for using the otpauth URI scheme to provision HOTP (RFC 4226) and TOTP (RFC 6238) credentials.
  
This document defines a common baseline for interoperability, including issuer handling rules that improve crdential matching while maintaining compatibility with existing deployments,
~~~
